projects.title: Sezo Audio Engine
projects.description: I needed an audio API for my Expo app with multi-track mixing and time/pitch shifting. On iOS, AVAudioEngine made this straightforward. On Android, there's no native advanced audio API—my only option was a professional SDK like Superpowered, costing thousands per year and total overkill for my needs. So I built Sezo Audio Engine. It includes two packages: an Android engine written in C++ published to JitPack, and an Expo module combining the Android engine with native iOS implementation, published to npm. Open sourced to save other developers the time and money I almost spent.

projects.title: ODEN - Open Data Developer Network
projects.description: ODEN was a large-scale collaborative effort to make open data more accessible. I worked in a team of 19, contributing to both the full-stack team and the tooling team. On the full-stack side, I built features using React, JavaScript, Google Cloud Functions, and a SQL database. On tooling, I helped create data pipelines along with validation and sanitization utilities. Working with such a large, cross-functional team was a great exercise in communication and coordination.

projects.title: YOLO Safety Helmet Detection
projects.description: An object detection system using YOLOv5 to identify safety helmets in images and video streams for workplace safety monitoring. Features model training on custom datasets, real-time detection via webcam, and deployment support for NVIDIA Jetson Nano edge devices.

image.alt: Safety helmet detection demo showing YOLOv5 predictions

projects.title: AI System Designer
projects.description: AI System Designer is a web app for AI-assisted system design with project workspaces, streaming chat, and generated assets like Markdown and Mermaid diagrams. It supports RAG-style context assembly, rate limits, and alerting for a production-ready workflow.

projects.title: Sing With Me (React)
projects.description: This was my first React project and the very first version of SingWithMe. It lets you break a song into individual lines with synchronized lyrics, so you can practice one segment at a time. You listen, record yourself, and compare. A simple loop that helped me improve my own singing. I built it to scratch my own itch, and it turned out to be a great way to learn React.

projects.title: Trip Monitoring Dashboard
projects.description: Developed a full-stack trip monitoring dashboard for a mining company as part of a 6-person team during a QDS hackathon. Analyzed big data and presented conclusions and predictions in an easy-to-use web interface. Implemented a REST API using Flask and Python and utilized Google Maps API to create a heatmap of truck locations. A data-driven solution for real-time trip monitoring.

projects.title: Sky Surfer
projects.description: Collaborated with a three-person team to build a Kotlin-based Android game inspired by Flappy Bird. Implemented MVVM to separate game logic from UI, a navigation graph with multiple fragments for smooth menu flow, and Firestore authentication plus leaderboard storage. Built core gameplay systems including frame-by-frame rendering and collision detection.

projects.title: CogniEasy
projects.description: CogniEasy is a lightweight GPT-powered tool that turns your resume and a job description into a polished, tailored cover letter. Built by a two-person team, it streamlines the application process with a clean, fast workflow.

projects.title: Inventory Manager
projects.description: This was my first real-world contract work. A friend of mine was starting up his car dealership; he had a neatly designed website built with GoDaddy's website builder, but was missing an inventory feature. I recruited my friend and classmate and we created the inventory manager using React and Firebase in a couple of months. It nicely fit the theme of the business's website, and I embedded it using an iframe. The business stopped using it as they no longer needed the inventory feature, but the whole thing is still functional, complete with an admin dashboard for adding and editing cars.

projects.title: Outliner Discord Bot (nwHacks2022)
projects.description: Outliner is a Discord bot that answers questions from BCIT course outlines using the OpenAI Answers API. Before ChatGPT and the official release of GPT-3, OpenAI was offering these more basic AI APIs and I couldn't wait to get some hands-on experience with them. So at nwHacks 2022, my team of four and I combined web scraping with a Discord bot server to create an AI chatbot with full knowledge of our course outlines. Of course, we didn't hesitate to ask it about the meaning of life; and it did not disappoint.

projects.title: Virtual Learning Buddy
projects.description: Virtual Learning Buddy (VLB) was my first introduction to web app style projects. I worked in a group of three to create a prototype of what the learning platform of the future would look like, with all the student's needs gathered in one place. We used Bootstrap for the styling, but the whole thing was still a vanilla web stack project. Little did I know this would be the last time I ever touched vanilla instead of frameworks.

projects.title: Arena of Blood
projects.description: Arena of Blood was my very first individual project when starting the Computer Systems Technology diploma. I created a text-based RPG adventure game using Python, complete with a full unit test suite for every function and comprehensive Python-style documentation. I remember getting carried away with this one when writing the story. It's definitely still worth a play. Can you find the secret ending without looking at the code?
